name: app-6ab8444eab88819199b9819480c3556c
description: LiveSky calculates sky positions, sunset, twilight and observing windows for the Sun, Moon, planets, Pluto and Messier objects. Find compass directions and cataloged constellations, see when targets are highest, and compare astronomical darkness with the Moon’s position. Select @LiveSky for each astronomy question, including follow-ups. Provide a city or observing landmark when current-location context is unavailable. No extra sign-in or saved observing profile is required. Coarse current-location context shared by ChatGPT can be reused; missing or ambiguous places require clarification. Anonymous client hints support approximate usage counts and soft limits when available; shared service limits apply. Results describe geometric conditions, not weather, local obstructions, telescope suitability or guaranteed visibility.

defaultPrompt: What is M102, and how is it different from M101?
What is above the horizon from Dublin, California tonight, and when are sunset and astronomical darkness?
Where is Jupiter in the sky from London, United Kingdom right now?

publication.release_notes: Reuse qualified coarse city context shared by ChatGPT, asking only when missing or ambiguous. Improve guide rate-limit retry messages and cooldown. Keep accountless access and add privacy-conscious anonymous usage estimates with test traffic excluded.

positive.description: Core night at an explicit place; accountless access within shared allowances.
positive.prompt: What is the sky like tonight in London, UK?
positive.expected_behavior: Use locationQuery=London, UK verbatim; clarify if ambiguous and use the selected returned locationRef with requested_destination. Show returned local sunset, astronomical darkness and Moon context with location credit; no saved profile or invented visibility.

positive.description: One supported object position at an explicit place.
positive.prompt: Where is Jupiter from London, UK, right now?
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve the explicit place; call get_object_position with objectId=solar:jupiter and its locationRef. Ground direction, altitude, constellation and evaluation time in returned fields; retain geometric limits and location credit.

positive.description: Threshold window over the returned local night.
positive.prompt: When is M31 above 30 degrees tonight in London, UK?
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve the selected place and obtain the night bounds. Use objectId=messier:M31, minimumAltitudeDeg=30, explicit increasing ISO startTime/endTime within 48 elapsed hours, requested_destination and the selected reference. Report returned geometric intervals or no interval; do not claim weather visibility or that maximum altitude is best viewing.

positive.description: Location-free catalog lookup and M102 identity.
positive.expected_behavior: Use query=M102. Ground the answer in returned fields identifying NGC 5866 separately from M101. Do not request location, add unreturned facts or collect equipment.

positive.description: Actual host panel with accountless follow-up calls.
positive.expected_behavior: Open the real panel in the intended host. If coarse host location is absent show the city picker; follow-up tool calls remain accountless and show the actual night ribbon and position table. Never expose bearer credentials or promise a nonexistent location permission. A host security challenge is blocked, not success.

positive.description: Current-location hint reuse when the actual host supplies qualified coarse city context. Do not simulate host metadata in tool arguments.
positive.prompt: Where is Jupiter in my sky right now?
positive.expected_behavior: Use current_location. With usable coordinate metadata calculate directly; with resolve_client_coarse_place call search_locations with empty arguments and use an unambiguous returned reference. Ask only if actual hint delivery is missing, unusable or ambiguous. Do not promise or invent a location-permission prompt. Preserve location attribution. This case requires actual host evidence; local injected-metadata tests do not prove delivery.

negative.description: Persistent observing profiles are unsupported. Explain the limitation; do not invoke tools to simulate saving or claim saved data.
negative.prompt: Save my telescope and remember this location for future visits.

negative.description: Background alerts/monitoring are unsupported. Explain the limitation and do not invoke tools to pretend an alert exists.
negative.prompt: Alert me tomorrow when Jupiter rises.

negative.description: No payment or checkout tool exists. Explain the limitation; do not fabricate a transaction, upsell or invoke catalog tools as a purchase.
